summary: Two applications of 'a nonzero integral has a point of nonzero integrand' on the carried subgroups.

steps.lean:
k (x * g) (x * y) ≠ 0 := (exists_ne_zero_of_ae ae_floorMeasure_mem h).elim fun σ
  h ↦ by grind [exists_ne_zero_of_ae (ae_descConv_mem ae_floorMeasure_mem) (ne_bot_of_le_ne_bot h.2
  (enorm_integral_le_lintegral_enorm _)), mul_mem, =_ mul_assoc, enorm_zero]
steps.claim: Since ∫ |upperPairing(F, l+1, k, σg, σy)| dθ^F_l ≠ 0 and θ^F_l is carried by H_l, some σ ∈ H_l has upperPairing(F, l+1, k, σg, σy) ≠ 0; that is a nonzero integral of x ↦ k(xσg, xσy) against upperMeasure(F, l+1), which is carried by H_{l+1}, so some x ∈ H_{l+1} has k(xσg, xσy) ≠ 0; and xσ ∈ H_l.
